# `aitbc bond lock-onchain`

Submit the on-chain BOND_LOCK escrow transaction for a provider bond. ``bond create``/``top-up`` record the bond coordinator-side but require a prior chain-verified ``BOND_LOCK``; this command is that missing leg. The tx pays ``--escrow-address`` (the node's ``BOND_ESCROW_ADDRESS``) with payload ``{bond_id, provider, lock_days}`` where ``provider`` is the signing wallet's own address — the chain refuses any other signer.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc bond lock-onchain [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--bond-id` | text | — | yes | Bond identifier recorded in the BOND_LOCK payload |
| `--escrow-address` | text | — | yes | Node BOND_ESCROW_ADDRESS — chain env config, not exposed via RPC |
| `--amount` | decimal | — | yes | AIT amount to lock into the bond escrow |
| `--lock-days` | integer | `30` | no | Lock duration in days (1-3650) |
| `--wallet` | text | — | yes | Provider wallet — payload.provider must equal the signer |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |
| `--rpc-url` | text | — | no | Blockchain RPC URL (default: resolved like transactions send) |
| `--format` | choice | — | no | Output format |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc bond lock-onchain --bond-id <bond_id> --escrow-address <escrow_address> --amount <amount> --wallet <wallet_name>
RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8202/rpc
aitbc bond lock-onchain --bond-id <bond_id> --escrow-address <escrow_address> --amount <amount> --wallet <wallet_name> --rpc-url "$RPC_URL"
```
